`quarto-simulator` is a teaching tool. It aims to render the documents a
learner writes while learning Quarto the way Quarto would, and to be honest
about where it can't. This page explains which parts are real Quarto, which
are simulated, and what that means for lessons.

## Real and simulated

`quarto render` is a TypeScript command-line program that runs knitr or
Jupyter, then pandoc with Quarto's Lua filters, then post-processes the HTML.
In the browser, pandoc and the Lua filters can run unchanged; the rest is
reimplemented:

| Step                      | `quarto render`                     | The playground                                                                     |
|---------------------------|-------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Parse YAML, build options | Quarto CLI (TypeScript)             | **Reimplemented**: [js-yaml](https://github.com/nodeca/js-yaml) plus a mapping of the options a playground document uses |
| Run R code                | knitr with Quarto's hooks           | **Reimplemented**: [webR](https://docs.r-wasm.org/webr/) plus an imitation of knitr that emits the same markdown and cell attributes as Quarto's knitr hooks |
| Run Python code           | Jupyter (an IPython kernel), then Quarto turns outputs into markdown | **Mostly real**: IPython in [Pyodide](https://pyodide.org), in a Web Worker, after Quarto's own kernel setup code. The outputs-to-markdown step is ported from Quarto |
| Markdown → HTML           | pandoc 3.10 with Quarto's Lua       | **Real**: pandoc 3.10 compiled to WebAssembly, with Quarto 1.10.19's reader, Lua filters, data directory, template and partials |
| HTML post-processing      | Quarto CLI (TypeScript)             | **Partly ported** from Quarto's source                                              |
| Page assets               | Bootstrap, `quarto.js` and so on    | **Real**: the files from a Quarto 1.10.19 render                                    |

The preview pane is labelled **Preview (simulated Quarto)** so learners know
what they're looking at.

## How close is it?

The project's tests compare the simulator with native Quarto 1.10.19:

- **pandoc's output is identical** for a document covering callouts, tabsets,
  subfigures, equations, theorems, margin content, footnotes, shortcodes,
  code annotations and an R figure. Warnings match too: `Unable to resolve
  crossref @fig-nope` comes from the same line of Quarto's `main.lua`.
- **Python documents render identical HTML** to Quarto with a Jupyter kernel,
  for documents covering printed output, expression values, warnings, errors,
  `eval`/`echo`/`output`/`include`, `echo: fenced`, matplotlib figures with
  labels, captions and subcaptions, pandas tables, `display(Markdown(...))`
  and inline `{python}` code. The exceptions are figure widths that can
  differ by a pixel, because fonts differ, and the file name in warnings.

Known differences in the final page:

- Three steps of Quarto's HTML post-processing aren't ported yet: margin
  columns (`column-margin`), code annotation markup, and the footnotes
  appendix. These render, but not exactly as Quarto lays them out.
- R output is an imitation of knitr; see [R code](r-code.qmd).

The page layout is Quarto's own, so it responds to the preview's width as a
browser window would. The table of contents, for example, sits in the right
margin (or wherever `toc-location` says) and, as in Quarto, is hidden when
the page is narrower than 768 pixels. The default side-by-side preview
usually is; a `layout: vertical` preview is wide enough in a typical lesson.

## Not supported

- **Output formats other than HTML.** For `format: pdf` and others, a notice
  explains that the preview shows HTML.
- **Themes.** `theme` has no effect; the preview always uses Quarto's default.
- **Projects and files.** Multi-file projects, local images and data files,
  bibliographies and `include` shortcodes.
- **Other engines and extensions.** Julia, OJS and third-party Quarto
  extensions.
- **YAML validation.** Quarto validates options against a schema in
  TypeScript; the simulator only suggests fixes for misspelled option names.

## Performance

Everything loads on first use and is shared by every playground on the page:

| Download                                | Transferred     | When                                  |
|-----------------------------------------|-----------------|---------------------------------------|
| The extension's own files               | about 4 MB      | First render on the page              |
| pandoc                                  | about 16 MB     | First render on the page              |
| webR and base R                         | about 14 MB     | First document with R code            |
| Pyodide, IPython, numpy and pandas      | about 16 MB     | First Python document that uses pandas |
| matplotlib                              | several MB more | First `import matplotlib`             |

The extension's files are smaller when the server compresses them, as
GitHub Pages does. Browsers cache all of these, so later visits are much faster. After the first
render, a render takes about half a second, most of it Quarto's Lua filters
starting up.

One quirk: a code block whose language pandoc knows only by an alias or not
at all (` ```md `, ` ```py `, ` ```sh `, ` ```js `, ` ```text `) makes that render about a
second slower, while pandoc searches its syntax definitions. Full names
(` ```markdown `, ` ```python `, ` ```bash `, ` ```javascript `) don't.

## Hosting and embedding {#hosting-and-embedding}

A lesson is a static site: any web server works, including GitHub Pages and
Posit Connect. It must be served over HTTP; a file opened from disk won't
work.

The browser needs ES modules, Web Workers, `fetch` to the hosts below, and
iframes with `srcdoc`. By default the binaries come from public CDNs:

| File       | Default                                                         | Setting           |
|------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| pandoc     | `https://unpkg.com/pandoc-wasm@1.1.0/src/pandoc.wasm`           | `pandoc-wasm-url` |
| webR       | `https://webr.r-wasm.org/v0.6.0/webr.mjs`                       | `webr-url`        |
| Pyodide    | `https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v314.0.7/full/pyodide.mjs`   | `pyodide-url`     |

For production, host `pandoc.wasm` yourself, compressed with gzip or brotli,
and set `pandoc-wasm-url` in the lesson's `quarto-simulator:` settings
(jsDelivr refuses files this large, which is why unpkg is the default).

If the host sets a Content Security Policy, it must allow scripts and
`fetch` from those hosts, `wasm-unsafe-eval`, workers from the site itself,
and `new Function` for checks (`unsafe-eval`).

## Versions

Quarto's Lua filters are written for a specific pandoc. pandoc-wasm 1.1.0 is
pandoc 3.10, which matches Quarto 1.10, so the bundled runtime is captured
from Quarto 1.10.19. When Quarto moves to a newer pandoc, the runtime has to
be rebuilt from that Quarto with a matching pandoc-wasm. The repository's
`CONTRIBUTING.md` explains how.
